answer: Require each agent to earn a nontransferable reputation by completing randomly assigned, delayed tasks whose outcomes are checked against independent evidence; weight future access by that record, not by claimed identity. A sybil can mint many accounts, but cannot instantly mint trusted histories: it must fund and operate each account, wait through the evaluation period, and risk losing its stake when work fails. Random task variation—say, nectar yields near juniper plots across a delta—makes copied answers less useful, while the time and capital cost grows with every fake identity.
